violations.title: Alarm.com control endpoints deployed without feature flag
violations.content: The `alarm_com.py` route module exposes high-risk security system control endpoints — `POST /partitions/{partition_id}/command` (`send_partition_command`) and `POST /locks/{lock_id}/command` (`send_lock_command`) — that arm/disarm alarms and lock/unlock physical doors. These are always-active with no toggle mechanism visible in the route registrations or service setters (`set_alarm_com_client`, `set_db`). Such irreversible, externally-visible actions warrant a feature flag for gradual rollout and emergency disable without a full code rollback.
violations.fixPrompt: Add a feature flag (e.g., env var `ALARM_COM_CONTROL_ENABLED`) checked at the top of `send_partition_command` and `send_lock_command` in `backend/routes/alarm_com.py`. Return HTTP 503 with a clear message when disabled. Optionally split read-only endpoints (status, sensors, devices) from write/control endpoints so they can be flagged independently.

violations.title: Unused `json` import
violations.content: `json` is imported in `routes/alarm_com.py` but never referenced anywhere in the file. Credential serialization is delegated to `store_encrypted_setting`/`load_encrypted_setting` from `utils`. Removing the unused import keeps imports tidy.
violations.fixPrompt: Remove the unused `import json` line from `backend/routes/alarm_com.py`.

violations.title: Alexa Lambda integration endpoints deployed without feature flag
violations.content: The `alexa.py` route module registers a large new Lambda/Smart Home control surface (`POST /lambda/token`, `POST /lambda/accept-grant`, `GET /lambda/discover`, `POST /lambda/refresh-cache`, `GET /lambda/state/{endpoint_id}`, `POST /lambda/command`, plus `/smart-home/*` control routes) that drives external Alexa Smart Home Skill v3 traffic and writes Deco WiFi settings via `_deco_wifi_write`. There is no visible toggle to disable this integration short of rolling back. A feature flag is warranted because misbehavior here can affect customer Alexa devices and rewrite Deco WiFi config.
violations.fixPrompt: Introduce an `ALEXA_LAMBDA_ENABLED` (and optionally `ALEXA_SMART_HOME_CONTROL_ENABLED`) env-var feature flag. Gate `lambda_*` handlers and `control_smart_home_device`/`_deco_wifi_write` in `backend/routes/alexa.py` so they return HTTP 503 when disabled. Surface the flag state in `get_alexa_status` so the dashboard can reflect it.

violations.title: Dead Alexa Smart Home discovery helpers
violations.content: The capability helpers `_cap_alexa`, `_cap_health`, `_cap_power`, `_cap_toggle`, `_cap_range`, `_cap_mode`, `_cap_scene` and the endpoint builders `_build_deco_endpoints` / `_build_chester_endpoints` are defined but never called anywhere in the module. Their only callers (`lambda_discover`, `lambda_refresh_cache`) were neutered to `raise HTTPException(status_code=503)` per the disable comment at lines 1228–1234. The code lingers as preserved scaffolding but is unreachable today, which dilutes the file (~150 lines) and risks bit-rot — e.g. the `_cap_*` helpers reference fields that may diverge from the live Alexa schema before the Lambda is re-enabled.
violations.fixPrompt: Remove `_cap_alexa`, `_cap_health`, `_cap_power`, `_cap_toggle`, `_cap_range`, `_cap_mode`, `_cap_scene`, `_build_deco_endpoints`, and `_build_chester_endpoints` from `backend/routes/alexa.py` (lines 1268–1536). If Lambda integration is being kept for future re-enablement, move the helpers to a separate `routes/alexa_lambda_disabled.py` module that is not imported until the feature is reactivated, so the live `alexa.py` only contains code that runs.

violations.title: Unreachable `_refresh_state_cache` and `_build_all_endpoints`
violations.content: `_refresh_state_cache` (1551) and `_build_all_endpoints` (1612) are async helpers with no in-module callers. The only route that would invoke them — `lambda_refresh_cache` / `lambda_discover` — was changed to unconditionally raise `503`. They also mutate module-level globals (`_state_cache`, `_state_cache_time`) that no other code reads, making the entire stateful cache pathway dead.

violations.title: `import_alexa_mac_addresses` does far more than import MACs
violations.content: The endpoint handler `import_alexa_mac_addresses` advertises a narrow scope (import MAC addresses) but additionally: writes `alexa_name` and `alexa_device_type` onto `network_devices`, inserts rows into `alexa_device_links`, and overwrites `network_devices.friendly_name` when the existing name looks generic (lines 822–855). Callers reading the name would expect a read-only import that backfills MAC columns, not a rename of arbitrary user-visible device names. The misleading scope is risky because a UI click labeled "Import MACs" can silently rename devices the user named manually if the prior name fell into the `generic_names` set.
violations.fixPrompt: In `backend/routes/alexa.py`, either (a) rename the endpoint/handler to something like `import_and_link_alexa_mac_addresses` and update the route path / OpenAPI summary / frontend caller accordingly, or (b) split the logic: keep `import_alexa_mac_addresses` as MAC-only writes to `alexa_devices.mac_address`, and move the link creation + friendly_name rewrite into a separate explicit endpoint (e.g. `auto_link_alexa_devices`) the user opts into.

@router.post("/import-mac-addresses")
async def import_alexa_mac_addresses() -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Pull MAC addresses from Alexa Echo/Fire devices and auto-link to network devices.

    # 2026-03-09: Rewritten to use /api/device-wifi-details as primary source.
    # Previous approaches (Endpoint API v2 connections[].macAddress and devices-v2 macAddress)
    # don't work for consumer accounts — Endpoint API returns 403 (needs ASP scope),
    # and devices-v2 macAddress field is always null.
    #
    # The undocumented /api/device-wifi-details endpoint (cookie-based, via alexapy discovery)
    # takes deviceSerialNumber + deviceType and returns the real WiFi MAC + ESSID
    # for physical Echo/Fire hardware. Groups and non-hardware entities return 400.
    # This successfully returns MACs for ~16 of ~30 devices (real hardware only).
    """
    if alexa_client is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail="Alexa client not initialized")

    # ── Primary source: /api/device-wifi-details (cookie-based, real hardware MACs) ──
    # Uses get_all_device_macs() which iterates devices-v2, calls device-wifi-details
    # for each, and returns normalized MAC addresses (aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff format).
    try:
        device_macs = alexa_client.get_all_device_macs()
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"get_all_device_macs() failed: {e}")
        device_macs = []

    # Convert to endpoint_macs format: (identifier, friendly_name, mac_normalized, device_family)
    endpoint_macs = [
        (dm["serialNumber"], dm["accountName"], dm["macAddress"], dm.get("deviceFamily", ""))
        for dm in device_macs
        if dm.get("macAddress")
    ]

    # Count total devices attempted (from devices-v2 list)
    total_devices = 0
    try:
        raw_devices = alexa_client.get_echo_devices_web()
        total_devices = len(raw_devices) if raw_devices else 0
    except Exception:
        pass

    source = "device_wifi_details" if endpoint_macs else "none"
    logger.info(f"MAC import: source={source}, total_devices={total_devices}, with_mac={len(endpoint_macs)}")

    if not endpoint_macs:
        return {
            "success": True,
            "source": source,
            "total_endpoints": total_devices,
            "with_mac": 0,
            "linked": 0,
            "named": 0,
            "note": "No MAC addresses found. The /api/device-wifi-details endpoint "
                    "only returns MACs for physical Echo/Fire hardware. Ensure Alexa "
                    "cookies are configured. Use Deco import for non-Alexa device matching.",
            "endpoints": [],
        }

    linked = 0
    named = 0
    matched = 0  # MACs that match a network_device

    logger.info(f"MAC import: db={'set' if db else 'None'}, endpoint_macs={len(endpoint_macs)}")

    if db and endpoint_macs:
        with db.get_connection() as conn:
            cursor = conn.cursor()

            # Ensure mac_address column exists on alexa_devices
            # (added by migration 007, but safe to ensure)
            try:
                cursor.execute("SELECT mac_address FROM alexa_devices LIMIT 1")
            except Exception:
                cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE alexa_devices ADD COLUMN mac_address TEXT")

            for serial_or_id, friendly_name, mac, device_family in endpoint_macs:
                # Store MAC on alexa_devices record (match by endpoint_id which may be serial)
                # Note: endpoint_id in alexa_devices may differ from serial number used here,
                # so this UPDATE may affect 0 rows — that's fine.
                cursor.execute(
                    "UPDATE alexa_devices SET mac_address = ? WHERE endpoint_id = ?",
                    (mac, serial_or_id),
                )

                # Match to network device by MAC
                cursor.execute(
                    "SELECT device_id, friendly_name FROM network_devices WHERE mac_address = ?",
                    (mac,),
                )
                row = cursor.fetchone()
                if not row:
                    logger.debug(f"No network device match for MAC {mac} ({friendly_name})")
                    continue

                net_device_id = row[0]
                net_friendly_name = row[1]
                matched += 1
                logger.info(f"MAC match: {mac} ({friendly_name}) -> network device {net_device_id} ({net_friendly_name})")

                # 2026-03-09: Write alexa_name and alexa_device_type to network_devices
                # (always overwrite with latest Alexa data)
                cursor.execute(
                    "UPDATE network_devices SET alexa_name = ?, alexa_device_type = ? WHERE device_id = ?",
                    (friendly_name, device_family, net_device_id),
                )

                # Auto-create link if the alexa device exists in DB
                # (serial_or_id may not match an alexa_devices.endpoint_id, so check first
                # to avoid FK constraint violations on alexa_device_links)
                cursor.execute(
                    "SELECT 1 FROM alexa_devices WHERE endpoint_id = ?",
                    (serial_or_id,),
                )
                if cursor.fetchone():
                    cursor.execute(
                        "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO alexa_device_links (alexa_endpoint_id, network_device_id, link_type) VALUES (?, ?, 'auto')",
                        (serial_or_id, net_device_id),
                    )
                    if cursor.rowcount > 0:
                        linked += 1

                # Apply Alexa name to network devices that are unnamed or have
                # generic names (e.g. "Amazon", "network device", "phone").
                # Alexa names like "Kitchen Echo" are more descriptive.
                generic_names = {"amazon", "network device", "phone", "unknown", "", None}
                if friendly_name and (net_friendly_name or "").lower().strip() in generic_names:
                    cursor.execute(
                        "UPDATE network_devices SET friendly_name = ? WHERE device_id = ?",
                        (friendly_name, net_device_id),
                    )
                    if cursor.rowcount > 0:
                        named += 1
                        logger.info(f"Named device {net_device_id}: '{net_friendly_name}' -> '{friendly_name}'")

            conn.commit()

    return {
        "success": True,
        "source": source,
        "total_endpoints": total_devices,
        "with_mac": len(endpoint_macs),
        "matched": matched,
        "linked": linked,
        "named": named,
        "endpoints": [
            {"endpoint_id": serial_or_id, "friendly_name": name, "mac_address": mac, "device_family": family}
            for serial_or_id, name, mac, family in endpoint_macs
        ],
    }

violations.title: Configuration scattered across modules with no central settings module
violations.content: The codebase has no centralized configuration module. Each file independently calls `os.getenv` with its own inline defaults, and configuration sources are mixed across at least three mechanisms: (1) environment variables via `os.getenv` in `backend/main.py`, `backend/db.py`, `backend/middleware/auth.py`, `backend/routes/alarm_com.py`, `backend/routes/alexa.py`, `backend/routes/oauth.py`, `backend/routes/settings.py`, `backend/services/alarm_com_client.py`, `backend/services/alexa_client.py`, `backend/services/chester_client.py`, `backend/services/hiboost_client.py`, `backend/services/polling_service.py`, and `backend/utils.py`; (2) database-stored encrypted settings via `load_encrypted_setting`/`store_encrypted_setting` in `backend/utils.py`, used by `routes/alexa.py`, `routes/alarm_com.py`, and `routes/settings.py`; and (3) a filesystem-based key file (`.credential_key`) handled in `backend/utils.py`. This makes it difficult to know which settings come from where, encourages duplication, and prevents validation at startup.
violations.fixPrompt: Introduce a centralized configuration module (e.g. `backend/config.py`) that loads all environment variables once at startup using `pydantic-settings` or a `dataclass`, validates required values, and exposes typed attributes. Refactor `os.getenv` call sites in `main.py`, `db.py`, `middleware/auth.py`, all `routes/*.py` modules, and all `services/*_client.py` modules to import from the central config. Keep encrypted-credential storage as a separate `SettingsStore` abstraction but make it the sole interface to DB-backed settings.

@router.post("/import-mac-addresses")
async def import_alexa_mac_addresses() -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Pull MAC addresses from Alexa Echo/Fire devices and auto-link to network devices.

    # 2026-03-09: Rewritten to use /api/device-wifi-details as primary source.
    # Previous approaches (Endpoint API v2 connections[].macAddress and devices-v2 macAddress)
    # don't work for consumer accounts — Endpoint API returns 403 (needs ASP scope),
    # and devices-v2 macAddress field is always null.
    #
    # The undocumented /api/device-wifi-details endpoint (cookie-based, via alexapy discovery)
    # takes deviceSerialNumber + deviceType and returns the real WiFi MAC + ESSID
    # for physical Echo/Fire hardware. Groups and non-hardware entities return 400.
    # This successfully returns MACs for ~16 of ~30 devices (real hardware only).
    """
    if alexa_client is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail="Alexa client not initialized")

    # ── Primary source: /api/device-wifi-details (cookie-based, real hardware MACs) ──
    # Uses get_all_device_macs() which iterates devices-v2, calls device-wifi-details
    # for each, and returns normalized MAC addresses (aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff format).
    try:
        device_macs = alexa_client.get_all_device_macs()
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"get_all_device_macs() failed: {e}")
        device_macs = []

    # Convert to endpoint_macs format: (identifier, friendly_name, mac_normalized, device_family)
    endpoint_macs = [
        (dm["serialNumber"], dm["accountName"], dm["macAddress"], dm.get("deviceFamily", ""))
        for dm in device_macs
        if dm.get("macAddress")
    ]

    # Count total devices attempted (from devices-v2 list)
    total_devices = 0
    try:
        raw_devices = alexa_client.get_echo_devices_web()
        total_devices = len(raw_devices) if raw_devices else 0
    except Exception:
        pass

    source = "device_wifi_details" if endpoint_macs else "none"
    logger.info(f"MAC import: source={source}, total_devices={total_devices}, with_mac={len(endpoint_macs)}")

    if not endpoint_macs:
        return {
            "success": True,
            "source": source,
            "total_endpoints": total_devices,
            "with_mac": 0,
            "linked": 0,
            "named": 0,
            "note": "No MAC addresses found. The /api/device-wifi-details endpoint "
                    "only returns MACs for physical Echo/Fire hardware. Ensure Alexa "
                    "cookies are configured. Use Deco import for non-Alexa device matching.",
            "endpoints": [],
        }

    linked = 0
    named = 0
    matched = 0  # MACs that match a network_device

    logger.info(f"MAC import: db={'set' if db else 'None'}, endpoint_macs={len(endpoint_macs)}")

    if db and endpoint_macs:
        with db.get_connection() as conn:
            cursor = conn.cursor()

            # Ensure mac_address column exists on alexa_devices
            # (added by migration 007, but safe to ensure)
            try:
                cursor.execute("SELECT mac_address FROM alexa_devices LIMIT 1")
            except Exception:
                cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE alexa_devices ADD COLUMN mac_address TEXT")

            for serial_or_id, friendly_name, mac, device_family in endpoint_macs:
                # Store MAC on alexa_devices record (match by endpoint_id which may be serial)
                # Note: endpoint_id in alexa_devices may differ from serial number used here,
                # so this UPDATE may affect 0 rows — that's fine.
                cursor.execute(
                    "UPDATE alexa_devices SET mac_address = ? WHERE endpoint_id = ?",
                    (mac, serial_or_id),
                )

                # Match to network device by MAC
                cursor.execute(
                    "SELECT device_id, friendly_name FROM network_devices WHERE mac_address = ?",
                    (mac,),
                )
                row = cursor.fetchone()
                if not row:
                    logger.debug(f"No network device match for MAC {mac} ({friendly_name})")
                    continue

                net_device_id = row[0]
                net_friendly_name = row[1]
                matched += 1
                logger.info(f"MAC match: {mac} ({friendly_name}) -> network device {net_device_id} ({net_friendly_name})")

                # 2026-03-09: Write alexa_name and alexa_device_type to network_devices
                # (always overwrite with latest Alexa data)
                cursor.execute(
                    "UPDATE network_devices SET alexa_name = ?, alexa_device_type = ? WHERE device_id = ?",
                    (friendly_name, device_family, net_device_id),
                )

                # Auto-create link if the alexa device exists in DB
                # (serial_or_id may not match an alexa_devices.endpoint_id, so check first
                # to avoid FK constraint violations on alexa_device_links)
                cursor.execute(
                    "SELECT 1 FROM alexa_devices WHERE endpoint_id = ?",
                    (serial_or_id,),
                )
                if cursor.fetchone():
                    cursor.execute(
                        "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO alexa_device_links (alexa_endpoint_id, network_device_id, link_type) VALUES (?, ?, 'auto')",
                        (serial_or_id, net_device_id),
                    )
                    if cursor.rowcount > 0:
                        linked += 1

                # Apply Alexa name to network devices that are unnamed or have
                # generic names (e.g. "Amazon", "network device", "phone").
                # Alexa names like "Kitchen Echo" are more descriptive.
                generic_names = {"amazon", "network device", "phone", "unknown", "", None}
                if friendly_name and (net_friendly_name or "").lower().strip() in generic_names:
                    cursor.execute(
                        "UPDATE network_devices SET friendly_name = ? WHERE device_id = ?",
                        (friendly_name, net_device_id),
                    )
                    if cursor.rowcount > 0:
                        named += 1
                        logger.info(f"Named device {net_device_id}: '{net_friendly_name}' -> '{friendly_name}'")

            conn.commit()

    return {
        "success": True,
        "source": source,
        "total_endpoints": total_devices,
        "with_mac": len(endpoint_macs),
        "matched": matched,
        "linked": linked,
        "named": named,
        "endpoints": [
            {"endpoint_id": serial_or_id, "friendly_name": name, "mac_address": mac, "device_family": family}
            for serial_or_id, name, mac, family in endpoint_macs
        ],
    }

violations.title: Configuration scattered across modules with no central settings module
violations.content: The codebase has no centralized configuration module. Each file independently calls `os.getenv` with its own inline defaults, and configuration sources are mixed across at least three mechanisms: (1) environment variables via `os.getenv` in `backend/main.py`, `backend/db.py`, `backend/middleware/auth.py`, `backend/routes/alarm_com.py`, `backend/routes/alexa.py`, `backend/routes/oauth.py`, `backend/routes/settings.py`, `backend/services/alarm_com_client.py`, `backend/services/alexa_client.py`, `backend/services/chester_client.py`, `backend/services/hiboost_client.py`, `backend/services/polling_service.py`, and `backend/utils.py`; (2) database-stored encrypted settings via `load_encrypted_setting`/`store_encrypted_setting` in `backend/utils.py`, used by `routes/alexa.py`, `routes/alarm_com.py`, and `routes/settings.py`; and (3) a filesystem-based key file (`.credential_key`) handled in `backend/utils.py`. This makes it difficult to know which settings come from where, encourages duplication, and prevents validation at startup.
violations.fixPrompt: Introduce a centralized configuration module (e.g. `backend/config.py`) that loads all environment variables once at startup using `pydantic-settings` or a `dataclass`, validates required values, and exposes typed attributes. Refactor `os.getenv` call sites in `main.py`, `db.py`, `middleware/auth.py`, all `routes/*.py` modules, and all `services/*_client.py` modules to import from the central config. Keep encrypted-credential storage as a separate `SettingsStore` abstraction but make it the sole interface to DB-backed settings.

violations.title: `optimize_network` does not optimize anything
violations.content: The method `optimize_network` in `deco_client.py` is named as if it triggers a network optimization on the Deco mesh, but per its own docstring ("The Deco LuCI HTTP API does not expose an optimize endpoint") it only re-fetches `admin/network?form=performance` and `admin/client?form=client_list`. Callers that expect this to actually reconfigure or optimize the mesh will be misled. The name should reflect what it does (e.g., `refresh_network_state` or `get_network_optimization_snapshot`), or the function should be removed if there's no optimization endpoint available.

Update any callers accordingly.

def optimize_network(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """2026-03-11: Trigger Deco mesh network optimization.
        The Deco LuCI HTTP API does not expose an optimize endpoint
        (only available via TMP/Tether app). We force a full refresh of
        performance + client data to re-evaluate current network state.
        """
        with _local_api_lock:
            local_client = DecoClient(
                local_endpoint=self.local_endpoint,
                use_cloud=False,
                verify_ssl=False,
            )
            local_client.username = "admin"
            local_client.password = self.password
            try:
                local_client.authenticate()
                perf = local_client._local_encrypted_request(
                    "admin/network?form=performance",
                    json.dumps({"operation": "read"})
                )
                clients = local_client._local_encrypted_request(
                    "admin/client?form=client_list",
                    json.dumps({"operation": "read", "params": {"device_mac": "default"}})
                )
                client_count = len(clients.get("client_list", []))
                return {
                    "error_code": 0,
                    "performance": perf,
                    "client_count": client_count,
                }
            finally:
                local_client.logout_local()

violations.snippet:
def get_devices(self, force_refresh: bool = False) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Get all Alexa devices with normalized structure.
        Tries web API first (returns ALL user's devices), falls back to skill discovery.
        """
        if not force_refresh and self._is_cache_valid():
            return self._devices_cache

        devices = []

        # Try web API first — returns devices from all linked skills
        try:
            raw_appliances = self.alexa_client.get_smart_home_devices()
            if raw_appliances:
                logger.info(f"Web API returned {len(raw_appliances)} appliances")
                devices = self._normalize_web_appliances(raw_appliances)
        except Exception as e:
            logger.warning(f"Web API device fetch failed: {e}")

        # Fallback to skill discovery directive
        if not devices:
            try:
                raw_endpoints = self.alexa_client.discover_devices()
                for ep in raw_endpoints:
                    capabilities = ep.get("capabilities", [])
                    cap_interfaces = [c.get("interface", "") for c in capabilities]
                    device_type = self._classify_device(cap_interfaces, ep)
                    is_echo = device_type == "echo"
                    device = {
                        "endpoint_id": ep.get("endpointId", ""),
                        "friendly_name": ep.get("friendlyName", "Unknown"),
                        "description": ep.get("description", ""),
                        "manufacturer": ep.get("manufacturerName", ""),
                        "model": ep.get("modelName", ep.get("model", "")),
                        "device_type": device_type,
                        "capabilities": cap_interfaces,
                        "is_echo_device": is_echo,
                        "display_categories": ep.get("displayCategories", []),
                        "last_state": None,
                        "state_updated_at": None,
                        "is_stale": True,
                        "raw_data": ep,
                    }
                    devices.append(device)
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning(f"Skill discovery also failed: {e}")

        # Persist and cache
        for device in devices:
            if self.db:
                self._save_device_to_db(device)

        self._devices_cache = devices
        self._cache_time = datetime.now()
        logger.info(f"Cached {len(devices)} Alexa devices")
        return devices

violations.title: Unused method `_build_node_client_index`
violations.content: `_build_node_client_index` is defined on `DecoService` but never invoked anywhere in the codebase. `get_nodes_with_details` now builds the `clients_by_node` mapping inline from `topology.get('node_clients', {})` (see lines 116–120), making this helper obsolete. Carrying ~70 lines of dead code adds maintenance burden and confusion about whether the alias-resolution logic is still authoritative.

Verify by grepping the repo for `_build_node_client_index` — no other call sites should exist. The current `get_nodes_with_details` builds `clients_by_node` directly from `topology['node_clients']`, so removing this helper is safe.
violations.snippet:
def _build_node_client_index(
        self, raw_nodes: List[Dict[str, Any]], raw_clients: List[Dict[str, Any]]
    ) -> Dict[str, List[Dict[str, Any]]]:
        """
        Build node_id -> clients mapping from noisy Deco payloads.
        Supports mapping by node ID and node MAC address.
        """
        node_index: Dict[str, List[Dict[str, Any]]] = {}
        node_aliases: Dict[str, str] = {}

        for raw_node in raw_nodes:
            node_id = str(
                raw_node.get("nodeID")
                or raw_node.get("node_id")
                or raw_node.get("deviceId")
                or raw_node.get("device_id")
                or raw_node.get("id")
                or raw_node.get("macAddress")
                or raw_node.get("mac_address")
                or "unknown"
            )
            node_index[node_id] = []

            for alias in (
                raw_node.get("nodeID"),
                raw_node.get("node_id"),
                raw_node.get("deviceId"),
                raw_node.get("device_id"),
                raw_node.get("id"),
                raw_node.get("macAddress"),
                raw_node.get("mac_address"),
            ):
                if alias:
                    node_aliases[str(alias).lower()] = node_id

        for raw_client in raw_clients:
            candidate_keys = [
                raw_client.get("nodeID"),
                raw_client.get("node_id"),
                raw_client.get("nodeId"),
                raw_client.get("connectedTo"),
                raw_client.get("connected_to"),
                raw_client.get("parentDeviceId"),
                raw_client.get("parent_device_id"),
                raw_client.get("apMac"),
                raw_client.get("ap_mac"),
            ]

            resolved_node_id = None
            for key in candidate_keys:
                if key is None:
                    continue
                key_text = str(key).strip()
                if not key_text:
                    continue
                key_lower = key_text.lower()
                if key_text in node_index:
                    resolved_node_id = key_text
                    break
                if key_lower in node_aliases:
                    resolved_node_id = node_aliases[key_lower]
                    break

            if not resolved_node_id and len(node_index) == 1:
                # Single-node fallback when client payload doesn't include node mapping
                resolved_node_id = next(iter(node_index.keys()))

            if resolved_node_id:
                node_index.setdefault(resolved_node_id, []).append(self._extract_client_details(raw_client))

        return node_index

violations.content: The expression `Math.max(0, Math.min(1, (power + 13) / 25)) * 220` uses two unexplained numeric literals (`13` and `25`) to normalize the dBm reading into a `0..1` ratio for the SVG arc. These values appear to encode signal-level boundaries (likely a minimum power of `-13` dBm mapped over a `25` dBm range) but neither the code nor a comment explains their meaning. Extracting `MIN_POWER_DBM` and `POWER_RANGE_DBM` constants would make the intent clear.

violations.title: Magic numbers `720` and `8760` obscure time-unit conversions
violations.content: The literals `48`, `720`, and `8760` in the nested ternary for the test-count label are unexplained. `720` represents hours in a month (24×30) and `8760` represents hours in a year (24×365), but a reader has to compute that mentally. Named constants like `HOURS_PER_MONTH` and `HOURS_PER_YEAR` would make the threshold and divisor purpose obvious.
violations.fixPrompt: Extract `720` and `8760` (and optionally `48`) into named constants such as `HOURS_PER_DAY = 24`, `HOURS_PER_MONTH = 720`, `HOURS_PER_YEAR = 8760` at the top of `SpeedInsightsPage.jsx`, then reuse them in the test-count label expression on line 357.

violations.title: Magic hour values in time-range picker
violations.content: The time-range options `[6, 12, 24, 48, 72, 168, 720, 2160, 8760]` and the threshold/divisor pairs `< 720`, `/ 24`, `< 8760`, `Math.round(h / 720)` rely on unnamed conversions between hours, days, months, and years. violations.title: Alarm.com control endpoints deployed without feature flag
violations.content: The `alarm_com.py` route module exposes high-risk security system control endpoints — `POST /partitions/{partition_id}/command` (`send_partition_command`) and `POST /locks/{lock_id}/command` (`send_lock_command`) — that arm/disarm alarms and lock/unlock physical doors. These are always-active with no toggle mechanism visible in the route registrations or service setters (`set_alarm_com_client`, `set_db`). Such irreversible, externally-visible actions warrant a feature flag for gradual rollout and emergency disable without a full code rollback.
violations.fixPrompt: Add a feature flag (e.g., env var `ALARM_COM_CONTROL_ENABLED`) checked at the top of `send_partition_command` and `send_lock_command` in `backend/routes/alarm_com.py`. Return HTTP 503 with a clear message when disabled. Optionally split read-only endpoints (status, sensors, devices) from write/control endpoints so they can be flagged independently.

violations.title: Alexa Lambda integration endpoints deployed without feature flag
violations.content: The `alexa.py` route module registers a large new Lambda/Smart Home control surface (`POST /lambda/token`, `POST /lambda/accept-grant`, `GET /lambda/discover`, `POST /lambda/refresh-cache`, `GET /lambda/state/{endpoint_id}`, `POST /lambda/command`, plus `/smart-home/*` control routes) that drives external Alexa Smart Home Skill v3 traffic and writes Deco WiFi settings via `_deco_wifi_write`. violations.fixPrompt: Introduce an `ALEXA_LAMBDA_ENABLED` (and optionally `ALEXA_SMART_HOME_CONTROL_ENABLED`) env-var feature flag. Gate `lambda_*` handlers and `control_smart_home_device`/`_deco_wifi_write` in `backend/routes/alexa.py` so they return HTTP 503 when disabled. Surface the flag state in `get_alexa_status` so the dashboard can reflect it.

violations.title: `import_alexa_mac_addresses` does far more than import MACs
violations.content: The endpoint handler `import_alexa_mac_addresses` advertises a narrow scope (import MAC addresses) but additionally: writes `alexa_name` and `alexa_device_type` onto `network_devices`, inserts rows into `alexa_device_links`, and overwrites `network_devices.friendly_name` when the existing name looks generic (lines 822–855). Callers reading the name would expect a read-only import that backfills MAC columns, not a rename of arbitrary user-visible device names. The misleading scope is risky because a UI click labeled "Import MACs" can silently rename devices the user named manually if the prior name fell into the `generic_names` set.
violations.fixPrompt: In `backend/routes/alexa.py`, either (a) rename the endpoint/handler to something like `import_and_link_alexa_mac_addresses` and update the route path / OpenAPI summary / frontend caller accordingly, or (b) split the logic: keep `import_alexa_mac_addresses` as MAC-only writes to `alexa_devices.mac_address`, and move the link creation + friendly_name rewrite into a separate explicit endpoint (e.g. `auto_link_alexa_devices`) the user opts into.
violations.snippet:
@router.post("/import-mac-addresses")
async def import_alexa_mac_addresses() -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Pull MAC addresses from Alexa Echo/Fire devices and auto-link to network devices.

    # 2026-03-09: Rewritten to use /api/device-wifi-details as primary source.
    # Previous approaches (Endpoint API v2 connections[].macAddress and devices-v2 macAddress)
    # don't work for consumer accounts — Endpoint API returns 403 (needs ASP scope),
    # and devices-v2 macAddress field is always null.
    #
    # The undocumented /api/device-wifi-details endpoint (cookie-based, via alexapy discovery)
    # takes deviceSerialNumber + deviceType and returns the real WiFi MAC + ESSID
    # for physical Echo/Fire hardware. Groups and non-hardware entities return 400.
    # This successfully returns MACs for ~16 of ~30 devices (real hardware only).
    """
    if alexa_client is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail="Alexa client not initialized")

    # ── Primary source: /api/device-wifi-details (cookie-based, real hardware MACs) ──
    # Uses get_all_device_macs() which iterates devices-v2, calls device-wifi-details
    # for each, and returns normalized MAC addresses (aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff format).
    try:
        device_macs = alexa_client.get_all_device_macs()
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"get_all_device_macs() failed: {e}")
        device_macs = []

    # Convert to endpoint_macs format: (identifier, friendly_name, mac_normalized, device_family)
    endpoint_macs = [
        (dm["serialNumber"], dm["accountName"], dm["macAddress"], dm.get("deviceFamily", ""))
        for dm in device_macs
        if dm.get("macAddress")
    ]

    # Count total devices attempted (from devices-v2 list)
    total_devices = 0
    try:
        raw_devices = alexa_client.get_echo_devices_web()
        total_devices = len(raw_devices) if raw_devices else 0
    except Exception:
        pass

    source = "device_wifi_details" if endpoint_macs else "none"
    logger.info(f"MAC import: source={source}, total_devices={total_devices}, with_mac={len(endpoint_macs)}")

    if not endpoint_macs:
        return {
            "success": True,
            "source": source,
            "total_endpoints": total_devices,
            "with_mac": 0,
            "linked": 0,
            "named": 0,
            "note": "No MAC addresses found. The /api/device-wifi-details endpoint "
                    "only returns MACs for physical Echo/Fire hardware. Ensure Alexa "
                    "cookies are configured. Use Deco import for non-Alexa device matching.",
            "endpoints": [],
        }

    linked = 0
    named = 0
    matched = 0  # MACs that match a network_device

    logger.info(f"MAC import: db={'set' if db else 'None'}, endpoint_macs={len(endpoint_macs)}")

    if db and endpoint_macs:
        with db.get_connection() as conn:
            cursor = conn.cursor()

            # Ensure mac_address column exists on alexa_devices
            # (added by migration 007, but safe to ensure)
            try:
                cursor.execute("SELECT mac_address FROM alexa_devices LIMIT 1")
            except Exception:
                cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE alexa_devices ADD COLUMN mac_address TEXT")

            for serial_or_id, friendly_name, mac, device_family in endpoint_macs:
                # Store MAC on alexa_devices record (match by endpoint_id which may be serial)
                # Note: endpoint_id in alexa_devices may differ from serial number used here,
                # so this UPDATE may affect 0 rows — that's fine.
                cursor.execute(
                    "UPDATE alexa_devices SET mac_address = ? WHERE endpoint_id = ?",
                    (mac, serial_or_id),
                )

                # Match to network device by MAC
                cursor.execute(
                    "SELECT device_id, friendly_name FROM network_devices WHERE mac_address = ?",
                    (mac,),
                )
                row = cursor.fetchone()
                if not row:
                    logger.debug(f"No network device match for MAC {mac} ({friendly_name})")
                    continue

                net_device_id = row[0]
                net_friendly_name = row[1]
                matched += 1
                logger.info(f"MAC match: {mac} ({friendly_name}) -> network device {net_device_id} ({net_friendly_name})")

                # 2026-03-09: Write alexa_name and alexa_device_type to network_devices
                # (always overwrite with latest Alexa data)
                cursor.execute(
                    "UPDATE network_devices SET alexa_name = ?, alexa_device_type = ? WHERE device_id = ?",
                    (friendly_name, device_family, net_device_id),
                )

                # Auto-create link if the alexa device exists in DB
                # (serial_or_id may not match an alexa_devices.endpoint_id, so check first
                # to avoid FK constraint violations on alexa_device_links)
                cursor.execute(
                    "SELECT 1 FROM alexa_devices WHERE endpoint_id = ?",
                    (serial_or_id,),
                )
                if cursor.fetchone():
                    cursor.execute(
                        "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO alexa_device_links (alexa_endpoint_id, network_device_id, link_type) VALUES (?, ?, 'auto')",
                        (serial_or_id, net_device_id),
                    )
                    if cursor.rowcount > 0:
                        linked += 1

                # Apply Alexa name to network devices that are unnamed or have
                # generic names (e.g. "Amazon", "network device", "phone").
                # Alexa names like "Kitchen Echo" are more descriptive.
                generic_names = {"amazon", "network device", "phone", "unknown", "", None}
                if friendly_name and (net_friendly_name or "").lower().strip() in generic_names:
                    cursor.execute(
                        "UPDATE network_devices SET friendly_name = ? WHERE device_id = ?",
                        (friendly_name, net_device_id),
                    )
                    if cursor.rowcount > 0:
                        named += 1
                        logger.info(f"Named device {net_device_id}: '{net_friendly_name}' -> '{friendly_name}'")

            conn.commit()

    return {
        "success": True,
        "source": source,
        "total_endpoints": total_devices,
        "with_mac": len(endpoint_macs),
        "matched": matched,
        "linked": linked,
        "named": named,
        "endpoints": [
            {"endpoint_id": serial_or_id, "friendly_name": name, "mac_address": mac, "device_family": family}
            for serial_or_id, name, mac, family in endpoint_macs
        ],
    }

violations.title: Deco network-mutating endpoints deployed without feature flag
violations.content: `backend/routes/deco.py` exposes mutating endpoints — `PUT /wifi-config` (`update_wifi_config`), `POST /client-mesh` (`set_client_mesh`), `POST /optimize-network` (`optimize_network`), `POST /rename-client`, `POST /auto-name-nodes`, `POST /nodes/refresh` — that change network state for all clients on the mesh. None of the route registrations show a toggle mechanism. WiFi config changes are hard to reverse (clients may disconnect), so a feature flag for the write/mutation endpoints is appropriate for safe rollout.

violations.title: Configuration scattered across modules with no central settings module
violations.content: The codebase has no centralized configuration module. Each file independently calls `os.getenv` with its own inline defaults, and configuration sources are mixed across at least three mechanisms: (1) environment variables via `os.getenv` in `backend/main.py`, `backend/db.py`, `backend/middleware/auth.py`, `backend/routes/alarm_com.py`, `backend/routes/alexa.py`, `backend/routes/oauth.py`, `backend/routes/settings.py`, `backend/services/alarm_com_client.py`, `backend/services/alexa_client.py`, `backend/services/chester_client.py`, `backend/services/hiboost_client.py`, `backend/services/polling_service.py`, and `backend/utils.py`; (2) database-stored encrypted settings via `load_encrypted_setting`/`store_encrypted_setting` in `backend/utils.py`, used by `routes/alexa.py`, `routes/alarm_com.py`, and `routes/settings.py`; and (3) a filesystem-based key file (`.credential_key`) handled in `backend/utils.py`. This makes it difficult to know which settings come from where, encourages duplication, and prevents validation at startup.
violations.fixPrompt: Introduce a centralized configuration module (e.g. `backend/config.py`) that loads all environment variables once at startup using `pydantic-settings` or a `dataclass`, validates required values, and exposes typed attributes. Refactor `os.getenv` call sites in `main.py`, `db.py`, `middleware/auth.py`, all `routes/*.py` modules, and all `services/*_client.py` modules to import from the central config. Keep encrypted-credential storage as a separate `SettingsStore` abstraction but make it the sole interface to DB-backed settings.

def optimize_network(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """2026-03-11: Trigger Deco mesh network optimization.

        performance + client data to re-evaluate current network state.

                        "last_state": None,
                        "state_updated_at": None,

def _build_node_client_index(
        self, raw_nodes: List[Dict[str, Any]], raw_clients: List[Dict[str, Any]]
    ) -> Dict[str, List[Dict[str, Any]]]:
        """
        Build node_id -> clients mapping from noisy Deco payloads.
        Supports mapping by node ID and node MAC address.
        """
        node_index: Dict[str, List[Dict[str, Any]]] = {}
        node_aliases: Dict[str, str] = {}

        for raw_node in raw_nodes:
            node_id = str(
                raw_node.get("nodeID")
                or raw_node.get("node_id")
                or raw_node.get("deviceId")
                or raw_node.get("device_id")
                or raw_node.get("id")
                or raw_node.get("macAddress")
                or raw_node.get("mac_address")
                or "unknown"
            )
            node_index[node_id] = []

            for alias in (
                raw_node.get("nodeID"),
                raw_node.get("node_id"),
                raw_node.get("deviceId"),
                raw_node.get("device_id"),
                raw_node.get("id"),
                raw_node.get("macAddress"),
                raw_node.get("mac_address"),
            ):
                if alias:
                    node_aliases[str(alias).lower()] = node_id

        for raw_client in raw_clients:
            candidate_keys = [
                raw_client.get("nodeID"),
                raw_client.get("node_id"),
                raw_client.get("nodeId"),
                raw_client.get("connectedTo"),
                raw_client.get("connected_to"),
                raw_client.get("parentDeviceId"),
                raw_client.get("parent_device_id"),
                raw_client.get("apMac"),
                raw_client.get("ap_mac"),
            ]

            resolved_node_id = None
            for key in candidate_keys:
                if key is None:
                    continue
                key_text = str(key).strip()
                if not key_text:
                    continue
                key_lower = key_text.lower()
                if key_text in node_index:
                    resolved_node_id = key_text
                    break
                if key_lower in node_aliases:
                    resolved_node_id = node_aliases[key_lower]
                    break

            if not resolved_node_id and len(node_index) == 1:
                # Single-node fallback when client payload doesn't include node mapping
                resolved_node_id = next(iter(node_index.keys()))

            if resolved_node_id:
                node_index.setdefault(resolved_node_id, []).append(self._extract_client_details(raw_client))

        return node_index

violations.title: `search_by_*` helpers do not restrict matching to the named field

violations.title: Unused `checksum` variable in `TSLPPacket.decode`

violations.title: `verify_share_response` mutates instance state
violations.content: The method name `verify_share_response` implies pure verification (returns bool), but it also mutates `self.stok` and `self.start_seq` unconditionally — even before the verification check, which means a failed verification still leaves the session token populated. Boolean-returning `verify*` functions with hidden side effects are easy to misuse.
violations.fixPrompt: Either rename `verify_share_response` in `backend/tmp_client.py:478` to something like `process_share_response` to reflect that it both stores the token and verifies, or move the `self.stok`/`self.start_seq` assignments to occur only after the `dev_confirm != self._expected_cB` check passes.

violations.title: Alarm.com control endpoints deployed without feature flag
violations.content: The `alarm_com.py` route module exposes high-risk security system control endpoints — `POST /partitions/{partition_id}/command` (`send_partition_command`) and `POST /locks/{lock_id}/command` (`send_lock_command`) — that arm/disarm alarms and lock/unlock physical doors. These are always-active with no toggle mechanism visible in the route registrations or service setters (`set_alarm_com_client`, `set_db`). Such irreversible, externally-visible actions warrant a feature flag for gradual rollout and emergency disable without a full code rollback.

Return HTTP 503 with a clear message when disabled. Optionally split read-only endpoints (status, sensors, devices) from write/control endpoints so they can be flagged independently.

violations.title: Configuration scattered across modules with no central settings module
violations.content: The codebase has no centralized configuration module. Each file independently calls `os.getenv` with its own inline defaults, and configuration sources are mixed across at least three mechanisms: (1) environment variables via `os.getenv` in `backend/main.py`, `backend/db.py`, `backend/middleware/auth.py`, `backend/routes/alarm_com.py`, `backend/routes/alexa.py`, `backend/routes/oauth.py`, `backend/routes/settings.py`, `backend/services/alarm_com_client.py`, `backend/services/alexa_client.py`, `backend/services/chester_client.py`, `backend/services/hiboost_client.py`, `backend/services/polling_service.py`, and `backend/utils.py`; (2) database-stored encrypted settings via `load_encrypted_setting`/`store_encrypted_setting` in `backend/utils.py`, used by `routes/alexa.py`, `routes/alarm_com.py`, and `routes/settings.py`; and (3) a filesystem-based key file (`.credential_key`) handled in `backend/utils.py`. This makes it difficult to know which settings come from where, encourages duplication, and prevents validation at startup.
violations.fixPrompt: Introduce a centralized configuration module (e.g. `backend/config.py`) that loads all environment variables once at startup using `pydantic-settings` or a `dataclass`, validates required values, and exposes typed attributes. Refactor `os.getenv` call sites in `main.py`, `db.py`, `middleware/auth.py`, all `routes/*.py` modules, and all `services/*_client.py` modules to import from the central config. Keep encrypted-credential storage as a separate `SettingsStore` abstraction but make it the sole interface to DB-backed settings.

violations.title: `import_alexa_mac_addresses` does far more than import MACs

The misleading scope is risky because a UI click labeled "Import MACs" can silently rename devices the user named manually if the prior name fell into the `generic_names` set.

violations.snippet:
@router.post("/import-mac-addresses")
async def import_alexa_mac_addresses() -> Dict[str, Any]:
    """Pull MAC addresses from Alexa Echo/Fire devices and auto-link to network devices.

    # 2026-03-09: Rewritten to use /api/device-wifi-details as primary source.
    # Previous approaches (Endpoint API v2 connections[].macAddress and devices-v2 macAddress)
    # don't work for consumer accounts — Endpoint API returns 403 (needs ASP scope),
    # and devices-v2 macAddress field is always null.
    #
    # The undocumented /api/device-wifi-details endpoint (cookie-based, via alexapy discovery)
    # takes deviceSerialNumber + deviceType and returns the real WiFi MAC + ESSID
    # for physical Echo/Fire hardware. Groups and non-hardware entities return 400.
    # This successfully returns MACs for ~16 of ~30 devices (real hardware only).
    """
    if alexa_client is None:
        raise HTTPException(status_code=500, detail="Alexa client not initialized")

    # ── Primary source: /api/device-wifi-details (cookie-based, real hardware MACs) ──
    # Uses get_all_device_macs() which iterates devices-v2, calls device-wifi-details
    # for each, and returns normalized MAC addresses (aa:bb:cc:dd:ee:ff format).
    try:
        device_macs = alexa_client.get_all_device_macs()
    except Exception as e:
        logger.error(f"get_all_device_macs() failed: {e}")
        device_macs = []

    # Convert to endpoint_macs format: (identifier, friendly_name, mac_normalized, device_family)
    endpoint_macs = [
        (dm["serialNumber"], dm["accountName"], dm["macAddress"], dm.get("deviceFamily", ""))
        for dm in device_macs
        if dm.get("macAddress")
    ]

    # Count total devices attempted (from devices-v2 list)
    total_devices = 0
    try:
        raw_devices = alexa_client.get_echo_devices_web()
        total_devices = len(raw_devices) if raw_devices else 0
    except Exception:
        pass

    source = "device_wifi_details" if endpoint_macs else "none"
    logger.info(f"MAC import: source={source}, total_devices={total_devices}, with_mac={len(endpoint_macs)}")

    if not endpoint_macs:
        return {
            "success": True,
            "source": source,
            "total_endpoints": total_devices,
            "with_mac": 0,
            "linked": 0,
            "named": 0,
            "note": "No MAC addresses found. The /api/device-wifi-details endpoint "
                    "only returns MACs for physical Echo/Fire hardware. Ensure Alexa "
                    "cookies are configured. Use Deco import for non-Alexa device matching.",
            "endpoints": [],
        }

    linked = 0
    named = 0
    matched = 0  # MACs that match a network_device

    logger.info(f"MAC import: db={'set' if db else 'None'}, endpoint_macs={len(endpoint_macs)}")

    if db and endpoint_macs:
        with db.get_connection() as conn:
            cursor = conn.cursor()

            # Ensure mac_address column exists on alexa_devices
            # (added by migration 007, but safe to ensure)
            try:
                cursor.execute("SELECT mac_address FROM alexa_devices LIMIT 1")
            except Exception:
                cursor.execute("ALTER TABLE alexa_devices ADD COLUMN mac_address TEXT")

            for serial_or_id, friendly_name, mac, device_family in endpoint_macs:
                # Store MAC on alexa_devices record (match by endpoint_id which may be serial)
                # Note: endpoint_id in alexa_devices may differ from serial number used here,
                # so this UPDATE may affect 0 rows — that's fine.
                cursor.execute(
                    "UPDATE alexa_devices SET mac_address = ? WHERE endpoint_id = ?",
                    (mac, serial_or_id),
                )

                # Match to network device by MAC
                cursor.execute(
                    "SELECT device_id, friendly_name FROM network_devices WHERE mac_address = ?",
                    (mac,),
                )
                row = cursor.fetchone()
                if not row:
                    logger.debug(f"No network device match for MAC {mac} ({friendly_name})")
                    continue

                net_device_id = row[0]
                net_friendly_name = row[1]
                matched += 1
                logger.info(f"MAC match: {mac} ({friendly_name}) -> network device {net_device_id} ({net_friendly_name})")

                # 2026-03-09: Write alexa_name and alexa_device_type to network_devices
                # (always overwrite with latest Alexa data)
                cursor.execute(
                    "UPDATE network_devices SET alexa_name = ?, alexa_device_type = ? WHERE device_id = ?",
                    (friendly_name, device_family, net_device_id),
                )

                # Auto-create link if the alexa device exists in DB
                # (serial_or_id may not match an alexa_devices.endpoint_id, so check first
                # to avoid FK constraint violations on alexa_device_links)
                cursor.execute(
                    "SELECT 1 FROM alexa_devices WHERE endpoint_id = ?",
                    (serial_or_id,),
                )
                if cursor.fetchone():
                    cursor.execute(
                        "INSERT OR IGNORE INTO alexa_device_links (alexa_endpoint_id, network_device_id, link_type) VALUES (?, ?, 'auto')",
                        (serial_or_id, net_device_id),
                    )
                    if cursor.rowcount > 0:
                        linked += 1

                # Apply Alexa name to network devices that are unnamed or have
                # generic names (e.g. "Amazon", "network device", "phone").
                # Alexa names like "Kitchen Echo" are more descriptive.
                generic_names = {"amazon", "network device", "phone", "unknown", "", None}
                if friendly_name and (net_friendly_name or "").lower().strip() in generic_names:
                    cursor.execute(
                        "UPDATE network_devices SET friendly_name = ? WHERE device_id = ?",
                        (friendly_name, net_device_id),
                    )
                    if cursor.rowcount > 0:
                        named += 1
                        logger.info(f"Named device {net_device_id}: '{net_friendly_name}' -> '{friendly_name}'")

            conn.commit()

    return {
        "success": True,
        "source": source,
        "total_endpoints": total_devices,
        "with_mac": len(endpoint_macs),
        "matched": matched,
        "linked": linked,
        "named": named,
        "endpoints": [
            {"endpoint_id": serial_or_id, "friendly_name": name, "mac_address": mac, "device_family": family}
            for serial_or_id, name, mac, family in endpoint_macs
        ],
    }

                        "capabilities": cap_interfaces,
                        "is_echo_device": is_echo,
                        "display_categories": ep.get("displayCategories", []),
                        "last_state": None,
                        "state_updated_at": None,
                        "is_stale": True,
                        "raw_data": ep,

def optimize_network(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """2026-03-11: Trigger Deco mesh network optimization.
        The Deco LuCI HTTP API does not expose an optimize endpoint
        (only available via TMP/Tether app). We force a full refresh of
        performance + client data to re-evaluate current network state.
        """
        with _local_api_lock:
            local_client = DecoClient(
                local_endpoint=self.local_endpoint,
                use_cloud=False,
                verify_ssl=False,
            )
            local_client.username = "admin"
            local_client.password = self.password
            try:
                local_client.authenticate()
                perf = local_client._local_encrypted_request(
                    "admin/network?form=performance",
                    json.dumps({"operation": "read"})
                )
                clients = local_client._local_encrypted_request(
                    "admin/client?form=client_list",
                    json.dumps({"operation": "read", "params": {"device_mac": "default"}})
                )
                client_count = len(clients.get("client_list", []))
                return {
                    "error_code": 0,
                    "performance": perf,
                    "client_count": client_count,
                }
            finally:

violations.title: Unused method `_build_node_client_index`
violations.content: `_build_node_client_index` is defined on `DecoService` but never invoked anywhere in the codebase. `get_nodes_with_details` now builds the `clients_by_node` mapping inline from `topology.get('node_clients', {})` (see lines 116–120), making this helper obsolete. Carrying ~70 lines of dead code adds maintenance burden and confusion about whether the alias-resolution logic is still authoritative.

Verify by grepping the repo for `_build_node_client_index` — no other call sites should exist. The current `get_nodes_with_details` builds `clients_by_node` directly from `topology['node_clients']`, so removing this helper is safe.
violations.snippet:
def _build_node_client_index(
        self, raw_nodes: List[Dict[str, Any]], raw_clients: List[Dict[str, Any]]
    ) -> Dict[str, List[Dict[str, Any]]]:
        """
        Build node_id -> clients mapping from noisy Deco payloads.
        Supports mapping by node ID and node MAC address.
        """
        node_index: Dict[str, List[Dict[str, Any]]] = {}
        node_aliases: Dict[str, str] = {}

        for raw_node in raw_nodes:
            node_id = str(
                raw_node.get("nodeID")
                or raw_node.get("node_id")
                or raw_node.get("deviceId")
                or raw_node.get("device_id")
                or raw_node.get("id")
                or raw_node.get("macAddress")
                or raw_node.get("mac_address")
                or "unknown"
            )
            node_index[node_id] = []

            for alias in (
                raw_node.get("nodeID"),
                raw_node.get("node_id"),
                raw_node.get("deviceId"),
                raw_node.get("device_id"),
                raw_node.get("id"),
                raw_node.get("macAddress"),
                raw_node.get("mac_address"),
            ):
                if alias:
                    node_aliases[str(alias).lower()] = node_id

        for raw_client in raw_clients:
            candidate_keys = [
                raw_client.get("nodeID"),
                raw_client.get("node_id"),
                raw_client.get("nodeId"),
                raw_client.get("connectedTo"),
                raw_client.get("connected_to"),
                raw_client.get("parentDeviceId"),
                raw_client.get("parent_device_id"),
                raw_client.get("apMac"),
                raw_client.get("ap_mac"),
            ]

            resolved_node_id = None
            for key in candidate_keys:
                if key is None:
                    continue
                key_text = str(key).strip()
                if not key_text:
                    continue
                key_lower = key_text.lower()
                if key_text in node_index:
                    resolved_node_id = key_text
                    break
                if key_lower in node_aliases:
                    resolved_node_id = node_aliases[key_lower]
                    break

            if not resolved_node_id and len(node_index) == 1:
                # Single-node fallback when client payload doesn't include node mapping
                resolved_node_id = next(iter(node_index.keys()))

            if resolved_node_id:
                node_index.setdefault(resolved_node_id, []).append(self._extract_client_details(raw_client))

        return node_index

violations.title: `request_otp` sends an OTP notification with no deduplication
violations.content: `request_otp` calls `alarm_com_client.request_otp(body.method)` which causes Alarm.com to deliver a one-time password to the user via app push, email, or SMS. There is no idempotency key, no rate-limiting, and no deduplication of recent OTP requests for the same `(user, method)` pair. A client retry triggered by a flaky network — or an automatic retry from the HTTP infrastructure — will cause a second OTP message to be sent to the user, which is annoying at best and can trigger upstream provider throttling/abuse detection at worst.
violations.fixPrompt: Add deduplication to `request_otp`. Track the timestamp of the last OTP request per `(session, method)` in memory or the DB and short-circuit (returning the cached prior response) if a request was issued within a short window (e.g., 30–60 seconds). Alternatively, accept and honor an `Idempotency-Key` header so retries of the same logical request never deliver a second message.

violations.title: `send_partition_command` arms/disarms with no idempotency protection
violations.content: `send_partition_command` dispatches `arm_away`, `arm_stay`, or `disarm` to a security alarm partition with no idempotency key and no check that the partition is not already in the requested state. While arming an already-armed partition is usually a no-op upstream, this is a security-critical mutation that frequently triggers audible chimes, push notifications, and audit-log entries on the alarm provider's side. If the request times out and is retried, the user receives duplicate notifications and the alarm audit log shows duplicate state-change attempts, which can mask real activity.
violations.fixPrompt: Make `send_partition_command` retry-safe. Either accept an `Idempotency-Key` header and cache the response keyed by it for a short window, or fetch the partition's current state before issuing the command and short-circuit (returning the cached current state) when it already matches the requested `arm_away`/`arm_stay`/`disarm` target.

violations.title: `import_alexa_mac_addresses` external API calls lack retry logic
violations.content: `import_alexa_mac_addresses` in `routes/alexa.py` calls `alexa_client.get_all_device_macs()` and `alexa_client.get_echo_devices_web()` against the external Alexa Web API. On a transient failure the function catches the exception and proceeds with `device_macs = []`, silently producing an empty import result instead of retrying. Given this is a manual user-initiated operation and the API is known to be flaky, transient failures should retry with exponential backoff before falling through to the empty-result path.

violations.title: `identify_complete` Deco API call lacks retry logic
violations.content: `identify_complete` in `routes/alexa.py` calls `deco_client.get_client_list_local` (an HTTP call to the local Deco router API) without retry. Any transient network error causes an immediate 500 response, requiring the user to restart the entire identify flow (which has a 5-minute snapshot window). Local-router API calls commonly experience transient failures and should retry with brief backoff.

violations.title: `import_alexa_mac_addresses` keeps iterating Alexa API on failure
violations.content: `import_alexa_mac_addresses` calls `alexa_client.get_all_device_macs()` which internally iterates `devices-v2` and calls `/api/device-wifi-details` for every device. There is no circuit breaker or maximum-failure threshold: if Amazon returns errors for many devices in sequence (e.g. cookie expiry, rate limiting, regional outage), the loop continues hammering the upstream endpoint and only catches a single top-level `Exception`. This can exhaust the shared `requests.Session` connection pool and amplify a partial Alexa outage into a full request stall on this route.
violations.fixPrompt: Add a circuit breaker / failure-budget around the Alexa MAC enumeration in `backend/services/alexa_client.py:get_all_device_macs` (or wrap it in `routes/alexa.py:import_alexa_mac_addresses`). After N consecutive `device-wifi-details` failures or a configurable error rate, abort the iteration early and return a partial result with an explicit `circuit_open` status so callers fail fast instead of continuing to call the failing endpoint.

violations.title: `_identify_snapshots` dict grows unbounded across `identify_start` calls
violations.content: The module-level `_identify_snapshots: Dict[str, Dict]` cache at line 960 stores a full Deco client-list snapshot (every online MAC + name + IP) per `entity_id` whenever `POST /smart-home/{entity_id}/identify/start` is called (line 990). Entries are only removed in two places: when `identify_complete` runs successfully (line 1064), and when `identify_complete` detects a stale snapshot (line 1019). There is no background sweep, no `__len__` cap, no LRU eviction, and the staleness check only fires when `identify_complete` is invoked. A client that repeatedly calls `/identify/start` with different `entity_id` values (or the same one without ever calling `/identify/complete`) will accumulate per-entity snapshots indefinitely. Each snapshot scales with the number of online network clients (potentially hundreds), so under abuse or buggy clients the dict can grow without bound and exhaust memory.
violations.fixPrompt: Add a bound on `_identify_snapshots` in `backend/routes/alexa.py`. Options: (1) enforce a maximum size (e.g. `MAX_IDENTIFY_SNAPSHOTS = 32`) and evict the oldest entry by `ts` before inserting in `identify_start`; (2) proactively prune entries older than 300s on every `identify_start` call rather than only inside `identify_complete`; (3) replace the raw dict with a TTL-bounded structure such as `cachetools.TTLCache(maxsize=N, ttl=300)`. Whichever approach you choose, ensure both stale-time AND maximum-cardinality limits are enforced regardless of which endpoint is called.

violations.title: Module-level discovery/state caches define `CACHE_TTL` but never enforce it

violations.fixPrompt: In `backend/routes/alexa.py`, either remove the unused `_discovery_cache`, `_state_cache`, `_discovery_cache_time`, `_state_cache_time`, and `CACHE_TTL` symbols (lines 30-35) if the disabled Lambda routes are not coming back, or wire up real invalidation: (1) add a helper `_cache_is_fresh(ts)` that returns `time.time() - ts < CACHE_TTL` and have any reader (including a re-enabled `lambda_discover`/`lambda_get_state`) call `_refresh_state_cache` / discovery rebuild when the cache is stale or empty; (2) call an invalidation function that clears `_state_cache`/`_discovery_cache` whenever Deco WiFi, node, or Chester state is mutated via the existing routes (`/api/deco/...`, `/api/chester/...`, settings updates) so source-of-truth changes do not leave clients reading 5+ minute old data.

violations.title: No error-monitoring SDK initialized in FastAPI backend
violations.content: The FastAPI entry point `backend/main.py` imports `fastapi`, `uvicorn`, `logging`, and the application's own modules but does not initialize any error-monitoring SDK (no `sentry_sdk`, `bugsnag`, `ddtrace`, or `opentelemetry` imports anywhere in the backend). All error handling routes through `logger.error(...)` only — see `routes/deco.py`, `routes/alexa.py`, `routes/events.py`, `services/digest_service.py`, `services/health_service.py`, `services/retention_scheduler.py`, etc. There is no global exception handler that ships unhandled exceptions to an external service, and no Express/FastAPI middleware that captures stack traces. Background tasks like `services/polling_service.py`, `services/hiboost_scheduler.py`, and `services/speedtest_scheduler.py` swallow errors with `logger.error(str(e))`, meaning failures in long-running async loops will only surface in local logs.
violations.fixPrompt: Add `sentry-sdk[fastapi]` (or an equivalent) to `requirements.txt`, initialize it at the top of `backend/main.py` using `sentry_sdk.init(dsn=os.getenv('SENTRY_DSN'), integrations=[FastApiIntegration(), AsyncioIntegration()])` guarded by the env var, and ensure background scheduler tasks (`hiboost_scheduler`, `speedtest_scheduler`, `retention_scheduler`, `polling_service`) report exceptions via `sentry_sdk.capture_exception(e)` in their error branches.

violations.title: No HTTP/DB performance metrics instrumentation in FastAPI app
violations.content: `backend/main.py` configures CORS, static files, and routers but never installs any performance-metrics middleware. There is no import of `prometheus_client`, `prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator`, `statsd`, `opentelemetry`, or similar across the backend. As a result, HTTP request latency, status-code distributions, and throughput per route (`/api/devices`, `/api/sse`, `/api/speedtest`, etc.) are not measured. SQLite query duration in `db.py` is unmeasured, and queue-style components like the SSE subscriber list in `routes/sse.py` (`_subscribers`, `asyncio.Queue`) and the background pollers in `services/polling_service.py`, `services/hiboost_scheduler.py`, `services/speedtest_scheduler.py` expose no depth/processing-rate gauges. Without metrics, regressions in scan time, speed-test cadence, or SSE backpressure will only be noticed when users complain.
violations.fixPrompt: Install `prometheus-fastapi-instrumentator` and in `backend/main.py` add: `from prometheus_fastapi_instrumentator import Instrumentator; Instrumentator().instrument(app).expose(app, endpoint='/metrics')`. Wrap key SQLite calls in `db.py` (or a thin helper) with a `Histogram('homesentinel_db_query_seconds', ['op'])` timer. Add gauges for SSE subscriber count in `routes/sse.py` (`Gauge('sse_subscribers').set(len(_subscribers))`) and for queue depths / last-run-age in `polling_service.py`, `hiboost_scheduler.py`, and `speedtest_scheduler.py`.

violations.title: No correlation/trace ID middleware registered in FastAPI app
violations.content: `backend/main.py` imports `fastapi.middleware.cors` and `middleware.auth` but registers no request-ID/correlation middleware. None of the route handlers (`get_devices`, `get_events`, `get_alerts`, `trigger_manual_scan`, `update_device`, etc.) accept a `Request` object to extract or generate a correlation ID, and there is no module-level extraction visible. Although `services.correlation_service` is imported, the absence of a global middleware means HTTP requests are not tagged with a trace ID that can propagate to logs, inter-service calls (`deco_client`, `chester_client`, `alexa_client`, `alarm_com_client`, `hiboost_client`), or SSE events.
violations.fixPrompt: Add a request-correlation middleware in `backend/main.py` (or `backend/middleware/`) that, for every incoming request: (1) reads `X-Request-Id`/`X-Correlation-Id` headers or generates a UUID, (2) stores it in a `contextvars.ContextVar` consumed by logging filters, (3) attaches it to the response as `X-Request-Id`. Register it via `app.add_middleware(...)` before CORS. Propagate the correlation ID into outbound client calls (`deco_client`, `chester_client`, `alexa_client`, etc.) via headers, and include it in log statements using a `logging.Filter` that injects `correlation_id` into each `LogRecord`.

violations.title: `create_device_group` is non-idempotent — retries create duplicate groups
violations.content: `create_device_group` is a POST endpoint that generates a fresh `uuid.uuid4()` server-side on every invocation and calls `group_repo.create_group` without checking for an existing group with the same `name`, and without accepting an idempotency key from the client. If the client (or any intermediate proxy/network layer) retries the request after a transient failure or timeout, a duplicate group will be created with a new ID but identical user-visible name. The frontend cannot safely retry a failed group creation without risking duplicate rows.
violations.fixPrompt: Make `create_device_group` idempotent. Either (a) accept an `Idempotency-Key` header, store the resulting `group_id` in a short-lived cache keyed by header value, and return the same response for repeated keys; or (b) enforce a unique constraint on the group `name` (per tenant) at the DB level and return the existing record's ID on conflict instead of creating a duplicate.

violations.title: `_call_backend` lacks retry logic on transient network failures
violations.content: `_call_backend` in `lambda/lambda_function.py` makes outbound HTTP requests via `urllib.request.urlopen` to the HomeSentinel backend (often through ngrok) with a 25-second timeout, but has no retry logic. Any transient failure — a TCP reset, DNS hiccup, 502/503 from an upstream proxy, ngrok tunnel restart, cold-start delay on the backend — immediately returns `None` and propagates as a failure to the Alexa Smart Home Skill caller. Because this code path serves voice commands (`turnOn`, `turnOff`, state reporting), a single transient blip results in a user-visible Alexa failure response. The function should wrap the `urlopen` call in a retry loop with exponential backoff (e.g. 2-3 attempts with jitter) for retriable conditions — connection errors, timeouts, and 5xx `HTTPError` responses — while still failing fast for 4xx client errors.
violations.fixPrompt: Add retry logic to `_call_backend` in `lambda/lambda_function.py`. Wrap the `request.urlopen` call in a loop that retries up to 3 times with exponential backoff (e.g. 0.5s, 1s, 2s with small jitter) on `URLError`, `socket.timeout`, and `HTTPError` with status >= 500. Do not retry on 4xx responses. Log each retry attempt. Keep the per-attempt timeout small enough that total time stays well under Lambda's execution budget.

violations.title: `_call_backend` lacks circuit breaker for backend HTTP calls
violations.content: The `_call_backend` helper makes HTTP requests to the HomeSentinel backend (potentially through `ngrok`) with a 25-second timeout, but has no circuit breaker. Each Lambda invocation independently attempts the call and logs failures, with no shared failure-rate tracking, no fast-fail state, and no cooldown. If the backend is down or slow, every Alexa Smart Home directive triggers a fresh 25s wait, exhausting Lambda execution time and the upstream connection budget. A circuit breaker that tracks consecutive failures and short-circuits to `None` for a cooldown window would fail fast and protect both Lambda and the backend.
violations.fixPrompt: Add a circuit breaker around `_call_backend` in `lambda/lambda_function.py`. Track consecutive failure count and a `cooldown_until` timestamp in module-level state (or DynamoDB for cross-invocation persistence). When failures exceed a threshold (e.g. 5 in a row), open the circuit and short-circuit subsequent calls to return `None` immediately until the cooldown elapses. Reset the counter on success. Consider using a library like `pybreaker` or `circuitbreaker`.
